'''Goaria''' is a [[Marwari language|Marwari]] language of the [[Rajasthani languages|Rajasthani]] branch of [[Indo-Aryan languages]], spoken by approximately 25,000 people in [[Sindh|Sindh Province]], [[Pakistan]].<ref name="Frawley">{{cite book |last1=Frawley |first1=William |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sl_dDVctycgC&pg=PA292 |title=International Encyclopedia of Linguistics |date=May 2003 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-513977-8 |page=292}}</ref> The Goaria people are predominantly [[Hinduism|Hindu]] and use [[Hindi]] for religious worship.<ref name="Frawley"/>

== Classification ==
Goaria is classified within the Marwari subgroup of the Rajasthani languages.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goaria |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/goar1239 |access-date=2026-01-28 |website=[[Glottolog]]}}</ref> It is one of several Rajasthani-related languages spoken by Hindu communities in Sindh, alongside [[Dhatki language|Dhatki]] and [[Marwari language|Marwari]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Literary notes: How many languages are spoken in Pakistan? |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1320097 |date=13 March 2017 |newspaper=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]}}</ref>

== Status ==
According to [[Ethnologue]], Goaria is a stable language with an [[Expanded Graded Intergenerational Disruption Scale|EGIDS]] rating of 6a (Vigorous), meaning it is used as a first language by all generations within the ethnic community.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goaria |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/gig/ |website=[[Ethnologue]]}}</ref> The language is not taught in schools.
